title: Walsingham to Burghley, Paris, 20 January 1572/3, letter-book copy, BL Harley MS 260 ff. 398-399 (DECODE R8363, catalogue item 123)

plaintext.source: No decipherment in the letter-book, in Digges 1655 (prints the cipher as cipher) or in CSP Foreign x.

transcription.notes: cipher.txt holds the target group (6 signs) and the one same-system group from Burghley's reply R8364 (6 signs). The letter is otherwise clear English.

system.summary: Place name written in digits and signs (2 1 ⌘ ε 9 4) inside a clear letter; a bracketed mark [9] stands where the copyist omitted another cipher name.
system.notes: Type 'homophonic' is inferred from the two groups (same first sign and third sign, different others); 12 signs cannot settle it.

prior_solution.where: Digges, The Compleat Ambassador (1655) p. 313 prints the letter with the cipher left in cipher type; CSP Foreign x no. 725 summarises a same-day letter without the passage.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: set up Claude Code with Opus 5 and posed the catalogue entry with /goal. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Fetched DECODE R8363 metadata and three full-resolution images with the saved cookie.
Read the three pages: a letter-book copy, clear English; the cipher is one six-sign place group plus a [9] placeholder on f. 398r.
Found the letter printed in Digges 1655 p. 313 (archive.org djvu text and page image): cipher printed as cipher, not read.
CSP Foreign x, January 1573 (BHO): no. 725 of the same day shares the opening, has no cipher passage.
Tomokiyo elizabeth.htm and DECODE key records searched for a Walsingham/Burghley key of 1570-73: none.
Applied the Cecil-Norris 1567-68 table (norreys1567): 'r a ? ? i p', nonsense.
Fetched sibling records R8356-R8364; viewed R8362 and R8364. R8364 (Burghley, Feb 1573) has one same-system group '2 0 ⌘ H 6 1' for a port.
Tested six-letter ports against the two groups under a homophonic alphabet: Dieppe, Calais, Nantes, Brest(e), Rouen(s) all fit; no reading can be chosen.

outcome.notes: Closed unread: 12 cipher signs in two letters, no key extant; Dieppe fits the context best but only as a guess (I).
